investigations.name: biogears-sbml-sepsis
investigations.title: Simulation core — one sepsis model, every engine: composed, ensembled, orchestrated, benchmarked
investigations.description: A guided tour of the simulation core's capabilities on one real model. The same BioGears sepsis core is run under three interchangeable engines (BioGears C++, exact SBML/Tellurium, PyTorch surrogate) and used to demonstrate four things, each a runnable artifact: COMPOSITION (study 01 — the same spec under three engines by one node swap), ENSEMBLES (study 02 — a severity × engine batch in one sweep), ORCHESTRATION/WORKFLOWS (study 03 — the four-verb API composes modules into a pipeline and hands an Antimony/SBML file between engines), and PERFORMANCE (study 04 — where the compute goes, and a ~40,000× surrogate tier). A fidelity backbone (study 05) keeps it honest: where the engines agree, and where they do not.
investigations.hypothesis:
This investigation is a capabilities DEMONSTRATION, not a single hypothesis test:
the thesis is that the simulation core already does all four of the above on a
real model, with each capability shown by an artifact that runs. The one place a
genuine hypothesis lives is the fidelity backbone (study 05): the SBML extraction
reproduces the inflammation core to within ~0.1% but diverges from the BioGears engine
in the hemodynamic layer — a real, measured result that keeps the demonstration
credible.
